document_title: The Trustees of Davidson College - Uniform Guidance Reports, June 30, 2024 (With Independent Auditors' Report Thereon) [FAC report 2024-06-GSAFAC-0000355426]
page: 5 (statement of financial position, printed p.3); 19 (note 7, printed p.17); 24 (note 13, printed p.22)
quote: Statement of Financial Position: current 'Notes payable (note 7) 14,335,000'; noncurrent 'Notes payable (note 7) 90,565,000'. Note 7: 'Senior Note (Series A), 2.46%, due March 1, 2050 $25,000,000'; 'Senior Note (Series B), 2.46%, due March 1, 2050 67,250,000'; '$30,000,000, unsecured Taxable Commercial Paper Notes, variable rate ... maturing no later than 270 days after the date of issuance of each note 12,650,000'; total '104,900,000'; 'Less current portion (14,335,000)'; 'Noncurrent portion $90,565,000'.
arithmetic: Long-term notes: Senior Note Series A 25,000,000 + Senior Note Series B 67,250,000 = 92,250,000. Bonds payable 0 and finance leases 0 (none on the balance sheet). long_term_debt_total = 0 + 92,250,000 + 0 = 92,250,000. Reported separately as short-term: commercial paper notes 12,650,000. Check: 92,250,000 + 12,650,000 = 104,900,000 = total notes payable in note 7 = 14,335,000 current + 90,565,000 noncurrent on the balance sheet (current portion 14,335,000 = 1,685,000 FY2025 senior-note principal + 12,650,000 commercial paper).
reporting_entity: The Trustees of Davidson College (the college itself; single-entity statements)
caveats: Confidence is medium only because of one classification judgment: the $12,650,000 of taxable commercial paper (maturities no longer than 270 days) is treated here as short-term borrowing and kept out of the long-term total, per the brief. The statements themselves present it inside 'Notes payable' and inside the five-year repayment schedule; if the workbook wants all notes payable, the figure is $104,900,000. All dollar figures were read directly from the audited statements. The senior notes are stated at principal; no premium, discount or issuance cost is shown in note 7. No finance leases, lines of credit or bonds are reported; note 13 discloses only 'Future minimum lease payments under noncancelable leases are $641,315' (not a recorded liability). Excluded: postretirement benefits other than pensions $15,253,696; supplemental retirement plan liabilities $1,368,162. Statements present FY2023 as summarized comparative information only. IPEDS $0 is a reporting gap, not a true zero. EMMA was not consulted.

quote: Statements of Financial Position: 'Long-term debt and accrued interest payable 18,028,475'. Note 8: 'In December 2018, Educational Facilities Revenue Bonds (2018 bonds) (with final payment due in June 2032) were issued in the amount of $24,415,000. reporting_entity: Gardner-Webb University (the university itself; single-entity statements)
caveats: The balance sheet shows one combined line, 'Long-term debt and accrued interest payable' $18,028,475, which includes $440,875 of accrued interest; accrued interest is not debt principal and is excluded from the value. Alternative presentations a reviewer may prefer: bond principal only $17,635,000; principal plus premium $17,885,225; balance-sheet line including accrued interest $18,028,475. Note 8 states management believes the University was in compliance with bond covenants at June 30, 2024; a $2,502,714 trustee-held reserve fund is included in restricted cash. The statements and notes contain no lease liability, line of credit or note payable (the word 'lease' does not appear as a liability anywhere in the document). quote: Statement of Financial Position liabilities: accounts payable, accrued liabilities, deferred revenue and deposits, gift annuities payable, liability under split interest agreements, and 'Lease liabilities 16,636,262' - no bonds, notes or long-term debt line. Note 10: 'On April 5, 2023, the University redeemed the entire outstanding principal of Series 2012 taxable bonds in the amount of $100,000,000 ... redeemed the entire outstanding principal amount of the Series 2019 taxable bonds in the amount of $89,750,000'; 'There was no interest expense during the year ended June 30, 2024 since the Series 2012 and Series 2019 bonds were redeemed in April 2023.' arithmetic: Bonds payable 0 (all bonds redeemed April 2023, i.e. in FY2023) + notes/loans 0 + finance lease liabilities (432,995 current + 7,822,987 long-term = 8,255,982) = 8,255,982. Check: finance 8,255,982 + operating 8,380,280 = 16,636,262 = 'Lease liabilities' on the balance sheet.

document_title: Lindenwood Education System - Consolidated Financial Statements, June 30, 2024 [FAC report 2024-06-GSAFAC-0000360701, filed under auditee name Lindenwood University]
page: 7 (consolidated statement of financial position, printed p.5); 41-43 (notes 16 and 17, printed pp.39-41); 48 (consolidating statement of financial position, printed p.46); 24 (lease policy, 'does not have any finance leases'); 11 (note 1, entity)
quote: Consolidated Statement of Financial Position: 'Lines of credit - [2024] / 7,960,000 [2023]'; 'Note payable 23,066,667'; 'Lease liabilities 21,019,622'. Note 17: 'In December 2023, the System issued tax-exempt bonds (the Bonds) through the Michigan Finance Authority totaling $24,163,000. The proceeds from the Bonds were utilized to retire the existing long-term note payable'; maturities total '23,223,328'; 'Less: unamortized costs of issuance 156,661'; '$23,066,667'. Note 16: 'As of June 30, 2024, the System had no outstanding borrowings under the line of credit.' Lease policy: 'The System does not have any finance leases.' Consolidating Statement of Financial Position, 'Note payable': Lindenwood Education System '-', Lindenwood University, LLC '-', Dorsey School of Beauty '-', Dorsey '23,066,667', System Total '23,066,667'.
arithmetic: Bonds outstanding 23,223,328 - unamortized costs of issuance 156,661 = 23,066,667 (the amount captioned 'Note payable' on the balance sheet; note 17 identifies it as tax-exempt bonds, so it is entered under bonds_payable). Notes/loans 0; finance leases 0 (statements say none). long_term_debt_total = 23,066,667 + 0 + 0 = 23,066,667. Line of credit drawn at 6/30/2024: 0.
reporting_entity: Lindenwood Education System (the consolidated parent, 'formally known as Lindenwood University'), which includes Lindenwood University, LLC plus Dorsey College Holdings and Lindenwood Holdings, LLC (Michigan career schools acquired March 2023). This is NOT a statement of the Saint Charles university alone.
caveats: HUMAN DECISION NEEDED - entity mismatch. The $23,066,667 is the consolidated System figure. The consolidating statement of financial position (supplementary information that the auditor reports is 'fairly stated in all material respects in relation to the consolidated financial statements as a whole') places the entire amount in the Dorsey column and shows NO note or bond payable and no line-of-credit balance in the Lindenwood University, LLC column; that column's only lease item is operating lease liabilities of $3,825,450. On that basis the IPEDS unit (Lindenwood University) would be $0 and the IPEDS $0 would not be a gap. Against that: note 17 says 'the System' issued the bonds and that they 'are secured by a pledge of the System's investments', and all $161,125,617 of long-term investments sit in the Lindenwood University, LLC column. The value entered is the consolidated audited figure; use $0 if the workbook wants the university entity alone. RubinBrown did not audit Dorsey College Holdings Inc. or Lindenwood Holdings, LLC; its opinion on those amounts 'is based solely on the report of the other auditors'. Other notes: the bonds were issued in FY2024 (December 2023) to retire a $24,000,000 bank note; the System reports it was in compliance with the bonds' collateral-value requirement at June 30; a $30,000,000 line of credit (expiring May 16, 2025) had no balance at 6/30/2024 (balance sheet shows $7,960,000 at 6/30/2023 while note 16 says $7,900,000 - a small inconsistency inside the document, prior year only). Excluded: operating lease liabilities $21,019,622 (all operating). Uniform Guidance compliance report in the same package is dated March 13, 2025. EMMA was not consulted.
form_990_crosscheck: ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer extract of IRS Form 990 for tax period ending 2024-06 (cross-check only, not audited): filer 'Lindenwood Education System' (EIN 43-0652649): tax-exempt bond liabilities $0; secured mortgages/notes $0; unsecured notes $0; total liabilities $20,979,818. The 990 for this EIN therefore carries no bond or note debt, which is consistent with the consolidating schedule placing the bonds in the separately incorporated Dorsey College Holdings rather than in the university entity.

quote: Balance Sheets (Dollars in Thousands): 'Line of credit payable (Note 7) 4,000'; 'Current portion of long-term debt (Note 8) -'; 'Current portion of leases (Note 9) 612'; 'Long-term debt, excluding current portion, net (Note 8) 106,364'; 'Long-term leases, excluding current portion, net (Note 9) 223'. Note 8: 'California Educational Facilities Authority 2023A Revenue Bonds ... The bonds are to mature in 2053. 110,000'; 'Principal outstanding on long-term debt 110,000'; 'Bond issuance costs (1,473)'; 'Bond discount (2,163)'; 'Total long-term debt, net 106,364'. Note 9 maturity table: 'Present value of lease liabilities 190 [Operating] 645 [Finance]'.
arithmetic: Statements are in thousands; converted to whole dollars (x1,000). Bonds: 110,000 - 1,473 issuance costs - 2,163 discount = 106,364 thousand = $106,364,000. Finance lease liability 645 thousand = $645,000. Notes/loans 0. long_term_debt_total = 106,364,000 + 0 + 645,000 = $107,009,000. Line of credit (separate, short-term) 4,000 thousand = $4,000,000. Check on leases: 612 current + 223 long-term = 835 = 190 operating + 645 finance.
reporting_entity: Saint Mary's College of California (the college itself; single-entity statements)
caveats: Amounts are rounded to thousands in the source, so the whole-dollar figures carry that rounding. Debt more than doubled in FY2024: on November 16, 2023 the College issued $110,000 thousand of CEFA Series 2023A bonds, used to retire the CEFA 2007 bonds ($51,675 thousand at 6/30/2023), pay off the line of credit, terminate the interest-rate swap (liability $5,524 thousand at 6/30/2023; nil at 6/30/2024) and provide working capital. Going-concern disclosure (note on printed p.29): conditions 'are possible indicators that substantial doubt about the College's ability to continue as a going concern exists in the absence of the implementation of an effective management plan'; the College 'concludes that management's plan alleviates the substantial doubt' and says it 'is dependent on the remaining $16,000 of bond proceeds for working capital' and Board-approved additional endowment spending. Covenant: cash and investments to debt of at least 0.75 to 1.00; 'in compliance, as determined by the bank' at June 30, 2024. Note 8 is internally inconsistent on descriptive details (purchaser named as U.S. Bank Trust Company in the table and Wells Fargo in the text; '20 year' bond that matures in 2053); this does not affect the amounts. Bond principal alone is $110,000,000. Excluded: operating lease liabilities $190,000; post-retirement benefits $1,664,000; asset retirement obligations $2,586,000; liabilities under trust agreements $1,884,000. The schedule of expenditures of federal awards in the package is dated March 25, 2025. IPEDS $0 is a reporting gap. EMMA was not consulted.

document_title: Connecticut State Universities - Annual Comprehensive Financial Report For the Year Ended June 30, 2024 (Connecticut State University System financial statements; includes Supplemental Information - Combining Schedule of Net Position by university)
page: 60 (combining schedule of net position - liabilities, printed p.59); 23 (statement of net position, printed p.22); 49-50 (note 14, printed pp.48-49); 29 (note 1, printed p.28); 37 (note 5 leases); 11 (auditor's paragraph on supplementary information); 65 (basis of presentation of supplemental information)
quote: Combining Schedule of Net Position, June 30, 2024 (columns CCSU / ECSU / SCSU / WCSU / SO / Combining 2024): current 'Bonds payable - / - / - / - / 21,370,000 / 21,370,000'; 'Note Payable - / - / - / - / 3,139,036 / 3,139,036'; 'Leases payable 156,255 / 57,495 / 62,316 / 64,394 / - / 340,460'; noncurrent 'Bonds payable - / - / - / - / 245,648,227 / 245,648,227'; 'Note payable - / - / - / - / 15,695,188 / 15,695,188'; 'Leases payable 214,670 / 24,694 / 84,655 / 18,700 / - / 342,719'. Note 1: 'The System Office administers certain activities centrally ... Primary among these activities are administration of certain system-wide information systems, telecommunications, capital projects planning and rebudgeting, technical support and debt service. Costs of such activities, including the allocation of funds to the Universities from bond proceeds, are included in the activity of the System Office'. Note 14: 'Principal outstanding of the CHEFA Bonds issued directly by CSUS at June 30 ... $257,955,000'; 'Total bonds payable ... $267,018,227'; State general obligation bonds 'do not require repayment by CSUS and, accordingly, the State's debt obligation attributable to the CSUS educational and general facilities is not reported as CSUS debt'.
arithmetic: No campus value computed. In the combining schedule the CCSU column shows no bonds payable and no note payable; the only debt-like item in the CCSU column is leases payable 156,255 current + 214,670 noncurrent = 370,925 (entered under finance_lease_obligations because GASB 87 does not distinguish finance from operating leases). System-level amounts, all carried in the System Office (SO) column and NOT allocated to campuses: bonds payable 21,370,000 + 245,648,227 = 267,018,227 (principal 257,955,000 + premium 9,458,276 - discount 395,049); note payable (installment payment agreement) 3,139,036 + 15,695,188 = 18,834,224.
reporting_entity: Connecticut State University System (four universities plus the System Office), an enterprise fund of the State of Connecticut; CCSU appears only as a column in the audited report's supplemental combining schedules. There is no separate audited CCSU statement.
caveats: The revenue bonds that finance CSU facilities are CHEFA bonds 'issued directly by CSUS' and are recorded entirely in the System Office column; the report gives no allocation of the $267,018,227 of bonds or the $18,834,224 installment note to CCSU, and none has been made here. State general obligation bonds for academic buildings are State debt and are not on CSUS's books at all. So IPEDS $0 for bonds/notes matches CCSU's stand-alone books, but CCSU's facilities are in fact supported by system-held and State-held debt. HUMAN DECISION: whether to show CCSU as system-held (value blank) or as $370,925 (its own GASB 87 lease liabilities only). The combining schedules are supplementary information; Grant Thornton states they are 'fairly stated, in all material respects, in relation to the basic financial statements as a whole'. Per the supplemental note they come 'from the stand-alone books and records of the universities and system office' and exclude pension/OPEB allocations. Excluded: CCSU subscription (SBITA) liabilities 755,557 + 876,792 = 1,632,349; system-level net pension and OPEB liabilities. Grant Thornton's opinion carries emphasis-of-matter paragraphs on presentation (enterprise fund of the State) and a change in accounting for fringe benefit expenses; neither affects debt. The document was read from CCSU's own website copy. The 'FY24 Annual Report' on ccsu.edu is the CCSU Foundation's donor report and contains no university debt data. The Connecticut Auditors of Public Accounts publish separate reports on CCSU; the latest one seen in search results is titled as covering FY2022-2023, it was not opened, and it is not an FY2024 financial statement. CHEFA/EMMA official statements were not consulted.
